title: Skeleton labelling sheet
subject: Science
unit: Spring 2: Skeletons, muscles, nutrition and plants (Tribal Tales)
source: Seeded from science/y3 lesson 7 (Skeleton labelling sheet (portal worksheet, printable or on a drawing tablet))
intro: Lesson 7: Skeletons: support, protect and move. To understand the three jobs our skeleton does for our body

picture.draw: Draw and label: Skeleton labelling sheet

questions.model: Think: where is the brain? In my head. What is the hard case round it? The skull. So the skull protects the brain.

questions.q: Name a joint in your arm.
Which job does the spine do?
questions.a: It supports us (holds us upright) and protects the spinal cord.

questions.q: Label the four bones on the skeleton sheet (skull, ribs, spine, leg bone) and write one job beside each.
questions.a: Skull: protect brain; ribs: protect heart and lungs; spine: support; leg bone: support and move
questions.model: Teacher labels the skull first and writes 'protects the brain' beside it.

questions.q: Find three joints on your own body and say which way each bends.
questions.a: For example: elbow bends one way; shoulder turns round; knee bends one way

questions.q: Why is a skull one hard piece but the spine is many small bones?
questions.a: The skull must be strong to protect the brain; the spine must bend, so it has many small bones.

questions.q: What are the three jobs of a skeleton?
What would you look like with no bones?
questions.a: We would be floppy, could not stand and our organs would not be protected.
